original_question: Fix an integer k > 2. Given a graph G as input, is deciding whether chi*_l(G) <= k complete for the complexity class Pi^P_2?
target_in_paper: Section 2, "Various open problems related to list packing," subsection "Computational hardness," Problem 2.10 on page 4: for fixed k>2, given a graph G, ask whether deciding χ^*_ℓ(G)≤k is Π^P_2-complete. ([researchgate.net](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/385898986_Open_problems_of_the_32nd_Workshop_on_Cycles_and_Colourings))
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper's official formulation almost verbatim: it fixes an integer k>2, takes a graph G as input, asks about the threshold condition χ^*_ℓ(G)≤k, and asks whether the resulting decision problem is complete for the class Π^P_2. That is exactly Problem 2.10. ([researchgate.net](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/385898986_Open_problems_of_the_32nd_Workshop_on_Cycles_and_Colourings))
missing_details: χ^*_ℓ(G) should be defined explicitly as the list packing number of G. ([researchgate.net](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/385898986_Open_problems_of_the_32nd_Workshop_on_Cycles_and_Colourings))

A k-list-assignment should be defined: the paper takes a list-assignment L of G to be a map L:V(G)→2^N, and a k-list-assignment means that every vertex receives a list of size k. ([researchgate.net](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/385898986_Open_problems_of_the_32nd_Workshop_on_Cycles_and_Colourings))

An L-colouring should be defined: it is a colouring c:V(G)→N such that c(v)∈L(v) for every vertex v. ([researchgate.net](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/385898986_Open_problems_of_the_32nd_Workshop_on_Cycles_and_Colourings))

Properness should be spelled out: an L-colouring is proper if adjacent vertices receive different colours. ([researchgate.net](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/385898986_Open_problems_of_the_32nd_Workshop_on_Cycles_and_Colourings))

Disjointness of colourings should be defined: two L-colourings c_i and c_j are disjoint if c_i(u)≠c_j(u) for every vertex u. ([researchgate.net](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/385898986_Open_problems_of_the_32nd_Workshop_on_Cycles_and_Colourings))

An L-packing of size k should be defined: it is a collection of k pairwise-disjoint proper L-colourings. ([researchgate.net](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/385898986_Open_problems_of_the_32nd_Workshop_on_Cycles_and_Colourings))

The quantifier structure hidden inside χ^*_ℓ(G) should be made explicit: χ^*_ℓ(G) is the least integer k such that every k-list-assignment of G admits an L-packing of size k. ([researchgate.net](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/385898986_Open_problems_of_the_32nd_Workshop_on_Cycles_and_Colourings))

For a fully stand-alone complexity question, the reduction notion behind 'Π^P_2-complete' is still implicit in the paper and should be stated explicitly if desired (standardly, polynomial-time many-one reductions). ([researchgate.net](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/385898986_Open_problems_of_the_32nd_Workshop_on_Cycles_and_Colourings))

It is also implicit that no extra restriction is imposed on the input graph in Problem 2.10; unlike nearby problems, this is asked for arbitrary input graphs G. ([researchgate.net](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/385898986_Open_problems_of_the_32nd_Workshop_on_Cycles_and_Colourings))
refined_question: Fix an integer k>2. For a graph G, let χ^*_ℓ(G) denote the least integer t such that every t-list-assignment L on G admits t pairwise-disjoint proper L-colourings c_1,…,c_t, where each c_i satisfies c_i(v)∈L(v) for all v∈V(G), adjacent vertices receive different colours in each c_i, and c_i(v)≠c_j(v) for every v∈V(G) and all i≠j. Given G as input, is the decision problem of whether χ^*_ℓ(G)≤k Π^P_2-complete (under standard polynomial-time many-one reductions)? ([researchgate.net](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/385898986_Open_problems_of_the_32nd_Workshop_on_Cycles_and_Colourings))
justification: The draft is already essentially the exact official wording of Problem 2.10. The only substantive issue is that it is not self-contained unless the paper's local definitions from the opening of Section 2 are inlined: list-assignment, L-colouring, properness, disjointness, L-packing, and the quantifier-heavy definition of χ^*_ℓ(G). The paper does not supply an equivalent reformulation of Problem 2.10, so the faithful refinement is just the same question with those definitions made explicit and no extra scope added. ([researchgate.net](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/385898986_Open_problems_of_the_32nd_Workshop_on_Cycles_and_Colourings))
